item.title: JPMorgan Chase v. Javice — via awesome-billing
item.description: Like Benford's law, applied to Excel: “JPMC first noticed irregularities with the list when a JPMC employee observed that the list contained exactly 1,048,576 rows, the maximum permitted by Microsoft Excel.” A count that stops at the limit of a tool is a sign of truncated or made-up data. Here, the executives of a startup sold for $175 million had bought that list of customers from a marketing firm.

item.title: Billing pipeline: a critical time sensitive system — via awesome-billing
item.description: Design notes on Scaleway's billing pipeline, built to “track nano-euros at the milli-seconds time granularity”. My takeaways: get the current time from one central method, randomize the order of the tests, and do not deploy in the first days of the month, when the accounting reports are produced.

item.title: source — via awesome-billing
item.description: ) - Mechanical Turk's rake was “20% (…) on the reward and bonus amount”, with a minimum fee of $0.01 per bonus payment, so a 7-cent bonus is billed one cent instead of 1.4: an effective 14.3% instead of 20%. The requester's round_payment() snaps every payout onto the 5-cent grid where that truncation always applies, and holds anything below 7 cents in the worker's wallet: “~$50 a day” saved. Rounding per transaction rather than per invoice hands the remainder to whoever picks the transaction amounts.

item.title: Blnk — via awesome-billing
item.description: 💸 Apache-2.0 double-entry ledger exposed as a REST API, with Go, TypeScript, Python and Java SDKs. Inflight transactions hold a pending leg until it is committed or voided, and the reconciliation engine matches external statements against custom rules. Blnk Finance sells a managed cloud adding back-office reports, audit logs and team permissions on top, but the core ledger, reconciliation and identity features are fully functional in OSS.
